projects.title: BRINDAVANA
projects.description: An expressive vertical urban residence in Bengaluru defined by textural buff brick cladding, sage green cantilevered balconies with cascading biophilic planters, and a sculptural spiral staircase leading to the entrance portal.
projects.processNarrative: Conceived as 'Brindavan'—a verdant garden sanctuary within the dense urban fabric—the residence layers vertical buff-brick tilework with tactile sage green stucco terraces. Cantilevered balconies burst with indigenous flora, creating a living microclimate that shields interior living quarters from street bustle while dappling tropical sunlight into double-height timber volumes. A floating external spiral stair ascends directly from street level to the arrival balcony, announcing the home with sculpted Kannada brass typography.

blog.title: Monolithic Concrete in Tropical Microclimates: The Poetics of Board-Formed Restraint
blog.excerpt: Exploring the tectonic and thermodynamic realities of cast-in-place concrete under South Indian monsoons and intense solar radiation.

content.introduction: Concrete in contemporary South Asian architecture is frequently misunderstood as a purely brutalist gesture. Yet, when modulated with regional awareness, board-formed concrete functions as an extraordinary climatic regulator, gathering cool night air and releasing it slowly across sweltering daylight hours.

sections.heading: The Dialogue Between Formwork and Finish
body: At Monolith House, our primary challenge was giving emotional warmth to cast walls without applying superficial cladding. We collaborated with regional timber yards to reclaim untreated pine boards with pronounced grain patterns. As the slurry settled, the wood sap and knots imparted an organic, tactile grain that softens the massive planes.

The concrete mix itself integrated 35% fly ash—an industrial by-product that not only reduces the carbon footprint of cement clinker but produces a denser matrix resistant to tropical water ingress during torrential monsoon seasons.
sections.quote: Architecture is not merely the envelope that contains space; it is the atmospheric medium that filters light, breeze, and the memory of time.

sections.heading: Courtyards as Thermodynamic Engines
body: A monolithic structure without intentional voids risks becoming an impenetrable heat trap. By hollowing the core with a deep basalt-lined sunken courtyard, we activated natural stack ventilation. Warmer air rises along the inner concrete clerestory and exhausts through continuous shadow-line vents, pulling cooler air across the ground-floor water body.
This simple physical mechanism maintains indoor ambient temperatures at 24°C to 26°C even when outdoor temperatures climb above 35°C in mid-April.

content.conclusion: When we treat concrete not as an industrial default but as liquid stone carved by timber and sun, architecture ceases to be an imposition on landscape—it becomes an organic extension of regional geology.

blog.title: Mass Timber in the Subtropics: Overcoming Humidity, Termites, and Tradition
blog.excerpt: How engineered glulam and cross-laminated timber (CLT) are pioneering carbon-negative commercial spaces in Bengaluru's tech corridors.

content.introduction: For decades, commercial construction in India has been synonymous with steel frames and glass curtain walls. However, the operational and embodied carbon penalties of these materials are no longer tenable. Our work on Timber Terrace proves that mass timber is both climatically viable and economically competitive.

sections.heading: Engineered Timber vs. Humid Climates
body: The prevailing myth against timber in peninsular India is rapid decay due to monsoon moisture and subterranean termites. By elevating the structural timber grid onto a 1.2m polished basalt podium, we physically disconnect the organic material from soil-dwelling pests.
Furthermore, non-toxic bio-based silane water-repellent impregnations permit the wood fibers to breathe without absorbing liquid water, maintaining dimensional stability across wet and dry cycles.
sections.quote: A steel beam represents energy consumed; a timber beam represents carbon captured and stored for a century.

sections.heading: Biophilic Productivity Gains
body: Beyond carbon balance, the biophilic advantages of exposed structural timber are profound. Sensor tracking in our prototype timber studios documented a 14% drop in baseline employee cortisol levels and measurably improved acoustic clarity compared to reverberant drywall enclosures.

content.conclusion: The architectural horizon belongs to hybridized structures where concrete anchors the earth, steel spans the extraordinary, and mass timber warms the human habitat.

blog.title: Sacred Geometry & The Controlled Infiltration of Daylighting
blog.excerpt: Choreographing shadows: How calibrated apertures and jali screens transform ordinary domestic volumes into contemplative sanctuaries.

content.introduction: In equatorial regions, light is not scarce; it is an overwhelming force that must be tamed, sculpted, and cooled before it enters our private spaces.

sections.heading: The Jali as a Spatial Filter
body: In Shadow House, our aperture placement was determined through solstice simulations. Rather than opening vast unobstructed glazed walls to the west, we deployed custom terracotta perforated modules with a 45-degree angled geometry that blocks direct afternoon sun while admitting soft ambient illumination.
The resulting patterns move across lime-plastered walls like a sundial, reminding inhabitants of the earth's quiet cosmic rotation.
sections.quote: Light does not simply illuminate space; light creates space.

content.conclusion: By designing with shadow rather than flooding every corner with glare, architecture returns to its primordial duty: offering shelter that restores the soul.

blog.title: The Architecture of Erasure vs. Preservation: Transforming Mid-Century Enclaves
blog.excerpt: Reflections on renovating historic brick fabrics in Bengaluru's Basavanagudi without resorting to nostalgic pastiche.

content.introduction: Basavanagudi is one of Bengaluru's quintessential historical neighborhoods, renowned for its stone rain trees, colonial bungalows, and conservative urban fabric.

sections.heading: Contrast as Respect
body: When we acquired the dilapidated 1960s commercial depot that now houses our principal studio, local advice was unanimous: demolish and build a generic multi-story glass box.

Instead, we chose radical preservation. We stripped away layers of acrylic paint to expose hand-made wire-cut bricks, reinforcing sagging timber rafters with slender black steel flitch plates. The new partitions are deliberately crisp and contemporary: fluted acoustic glass and anodized aluminium that never feigns to be vintage.

content.conclusion: Authentic respect for heritage lies in creating an honest, articulate contrast between what was and what is.

faq.question: What types of projects does Techno Architecture undertake
faq.answer: We provide end to end architecture, interior design and structural design services. Our portfolio includes residential, commercial, hospitality and bespoke interior architecture projects. Where additional expertise is required, we can introduce clients to suitable specialist consultants according to the project's scale and technical needs.

faq.question: When should we appoint an architect
faq.answer: The best time is before major decisions are made about planning, area, budget or construction. Early involvement allows the design team to study the site, clarify priorities and identify constraints before they become costly to change.

faq.question: What information should we share for an initial discussion
faq.answer: Please share your name, email address and contact number. A senior architect will get in touch directly to understand the requirements and discuss taking up the new project.

faq.question: Can you provide architecture and interiors together
faq.answer: Yes. An integrated appointment can help the building, interiors, lighting, materials and furniture develop as one coordinated design. The exact scope will be defined in the project proposal.

faq.question: Do you work on renovations
faq.answer: Renovation and adaptive reuse projects can be considered after reviewing the existing building, required changes and available documentation. A site assessment may be needed before the scope and feasibility can be confirmed.

faq.question: How does the design process begin
faq.answer: The process usually begins with a consultation, brief development and review of the site information. We then define the scope, deliverables, stages and professional fees before design work starts.

faq.question: How long does a project take
faq.answer: Timelines vary with project scale, approvals, design decisions, consultant coordination and construction conditions. We provide a stage-based programme after understanding the project requirements.

faq.question: How are professional fees calculated
faq.answer: Fees depend on the project type, size, complexity, location and scope of services. A detailed proposal is issued after the initial project discussion.

faq.question: Do you supervise construction
faq.answer: Construction-stage involvement depends on the agreed appointment. It may include periodic site reviews, drawing clarifications, consultant coordination and review of design intent. This is different from continuous site supervision unless specifically included.

faq.question: How do you approach sustainable design
faq.answer: We begin with practical measures such as orientation, daylight, ventilation, shading, efficient planning, durable materials and resource-conscious structural systems. Appropriate strategies are selected for the site, climate, budget and project goals.

faq.question: Can you work outside your home city
faq.answer: Projects in other locations may be undertaken depending on their scope, programme and travel requirements. Please share the site location during the initial enquiry so the appropriate service structure can be discussed.

faq.question: How can we start a project with Techno Architecture
faq.answer: Use the project enquiry form or contact the studio directly. A senior architect will get in touch to understand the requirements, confirm availability and discuss the next steps for taking up the project.

testimonials.quote: Living in Aikya has transformed our daily relationship with light and nature. Even during the peak of summer, the serene water courts and double-height living areas create an astonishingly cool, harmonious atmosphere. Techno's obsession with every millimeter of craft is evident everywhere you look.

Techno created a private urban sanctuary that dances with natural light throughout the day. The interplay of cantilevered concrete, corten steel, and sculptural timber screens makes Belaku an architectural masterwork we are proud to call home.

Techno designed a home that feels like a sacred sanctuary cradled by our centenary trees. The four-pillared inner mandapa courtyard and brick jali light create a living experience of timeless elegance.

The play of shadows cast by the terracotta jali and the lush cantilevered terraces make this home feel like a personal sanctuary in the city. Techno Architecture's vision featured on Buildofy is truly exemplary.
